MEETING ASSISTANCE NOTICE: In accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, services are available to members
of our community who require special assistance to participate in public meetings. If you require special assistance,
48-hour prior notification will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements for an assisted listening device (ALD) for the
hearing impaired, American Sign Language interpreters, a reader during the meeting and/or large print agendas. Please
contact the City Clerk’s Office at (714) 536-5227 for more information, or request assistance from the staff or
Sergeant-at-Arms at the meeting.

PUBLIC COMMENTS: To address the legislative body on items of interest not scheduled for public hearing, Request to
Speak forms will be made available at the meeting and are collected by the staff or Sergeant at Arms. Some legislative
bodies may provide different Request to Speak forms for public hearing items.

AUDIO/VIDEO ACCESS TO BROADCASTED MEETINGS: City Council and Planning Commission meetings are televised live
on HBTV-3 Channel 3, and can be viewed via live or archived website at https://huntingtonbeach.legistar.com.

PUBLIC COMMENTS PERTAINING TO CLOSED SESSION ITEMS (3 Minute Time Limit) - At
approximately 4:00 PM, individuals wishing to provide a comment on item(s) scheduled for Closed
Session may do so either in person by filling out a Request to Speak form, via computer through
Zoom Webinar ID 971 5413 0528, or Zoom Webinar by phone by calling (669) 900-6833 (see agenda
cover sheet for request to speak instructions). Zoom Webinar participants wishing to speak
should “raise their hands,” and will be prompted to speak when the Clerk announces their name
or the last three digits of their phone number. All speakers are encouraged, but not required to
identify themselves by name. Speakers providing comments in person will be called to speak first,
and each speaker may have up to 3 minutes unless the volume of speakers warrants reducing the
time allowance.

While the City Council welcomes public involvement and free speech, it rejects comments from

Approve the appointment of Sean Joyce as Interim City Manager. - Action: approved (Pass) Moved by Mike Posey {\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252\deff0\deflang1033{\fonttbl{\f0\fnil\fcharset0 Arial;}} {\colortbl ;\red0\green0\blue0;} \viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 City Manager Oliver Chi introduced this item by briefly describing the process and qualifications of Mr. Sean Joyce. Highlights of the employment contract were also covered, including there are no benefits other than salary, the contract can be terminated at any time based on the Council's desire, and no severance considerations.\par \par Mr. Joyce expressed appreciation for the opportunity to serve as Interim City Manager, and stated his commitment to work with Council and staff to achieve every aspiration for the community.\par \par Councilmember Posey stated that Mr. Joyce's reputation stands out, especially his service of 12 years in Irvine which means working with about six different councils, and stated his support for the appointment.\par \par Councilmember Carr expressed her appreciation that such a well-qualified individual has agreed to serve, which will certainly take some of the pressure off as Council works to find a new City Manager.\par \par Councilmember Kalmick thanked Mr. Joyce for stepping forward and stated his support for this appointment.\par \par Councilmember Moser thanked Mr. Joyce for his willingness to step up and support the City's exceptional staff to continue serving the community.\par \par Mayor Delgleize provided Mr. Joyce the opportunity to introduce his wife, Veronica.\par } 3.. Consider a declaration of a local emergency in Huntington Beach with regards to the current refuse service impacts in the City by adopting Resolution No. 2021-77 - Action: approved (Pass) Moved by Dan Kalmick {\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252\deff0\deflang1033{\fonttbl{\f0\fnil\fcharset0 Arial;}} {\colortbl ;\red0\green0\blue0;} \viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 Chris Kentauck, General Manager, Republic Services, was called to speak and stated Republic Services values its relationship with Huntington Beach, as well as the rights of their employees for collective bargaining, and are encouraged by the progress made today. Mr. Kentauck also stated that during negotiations Republic is using their emergency response team members to provide continued service to critical infrastructures like hospitals, assisted care facilities and schools, and are bringing in other staff to address residential needs. Mr. Kentauck stated his opinion that if a third party hauler is brought in, it will only create additional confusion and disruption. He closed his comments stating Republic is optimistic based on conversations with the Teamsters today and look forward to resuming full service as quickly as possible.\par \par City Manager Chi and Director of Public Works Sean Crumby presented a PowerPoint communication titled "Consideration of Declaration of a Local Emergency" with slides entitled: Trash Service Disruption Overview, City Response Issued on December 11, 2021; City Develops Trash Disruption Mitigation Response Plan; Additional HB Support Provided; Trash Services Update; Temporary Trash Drop-Off Locations; and Questions?\par \par Mayor Pro Tem Posey thanked the Teamster Representatives and Mr. Kentauck for their positive and encouraging reports. Councilmember Posey added that declaring a local emergency, with regards to the current refuse service impacts in Huntington Beach, is a proactive step by delegating to staff the ability to exercise an alternate carrier appointment if necessary. Councilmember Posey stated his support for giving staff the authority in case it needs to be exercised.\par \par Councilmember Kalmick thanked staff for stepping forward to address options under these unexpected circumstances, and stated his support for Mayor Pro Tem Posey's comments. He also stated that it is obvious that the City needs to develop a better method for community-wide communication for non-emergency messages.\par \par Councilmember Carr thanked Teamster Representatives Ms. Gonzales and Ms. Barnes, and Republic General Manager Kentauck for taking the time to attend this meeting and sharing their positive comments. She also stated her support for being proactive and having a plan of action in place if it is needed for this health and safety issue. Councilmember Carr stated her support for getting progress details out to the residents as timely as possible.\par \par Councilmember Moser stated her appreciation for representatives stepping up this evening with positive reports, and thanked staff for being proactive under the circumstances. She also stated this situation highlights the need for better communication with residents.\par \par Councilmember Moser confirmed with City Manager Chi that the issue of making residents whole from this disruption of service will be an important part of the conversation with Republic Services after the labor negotiations are completed.\par \par Councilmember Bolton stated support for the comment of her colleagues, and added that from her perspective communication on this issue from Republic Services has been confusing, fragmented, and chaotic. She further stated that a work stoppage is not the only potential reason for lack of trash pick-up, and expressed her expectation that Republic Services will make a better effort to share pertinent details for the residents.\par \par Mayor Carr stated her appreciation for the attendance of the Teamster's Representatives as well as Republic Services General Manager, and called for a motion.\par } COUNCILMEMBER COMMENTS (Not Agendized) ADJOURNMENT - 5:21 PM The next regularly scheduled meeting of the Huntington Beach City Council/Public Financing Authority is Tuesday, December 21, 2022, at 4:00 PM in the Civic Center Council Chambers, 2000 Main Street, Huntington Beach, California.
